chunks: My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash'ari, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Husayn al-Lu'lu'i, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yusuf, from Mu'az ibn al-Juhari, from Amr ibn Jami'a, who linked it up to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family).

He said: In the toothbrush (siwak) there are twelve attributes: it purifies the mouth, pleases the Lord, whitens the teeth, removes cavities and reduces phlegm, stimulates the appetite, multiplies good deeds, the Sunnah is attained through it, the angels attend to it, it strengthens the gums, and it cleans what you recite the Quran with. Also, two units of prayer said after using a siwak are more beloved to God, the Exalted, than seventy units of prayer said without using a siwak.

key_terms.السِّوَاك: Toothbrush or twig used for oral hygiene and ritual purity
key_terms.تُصَابُ بِهِ السُّنَّةُ: The Sunnah is attained/achieved through it

ai.seo_question: What are the twelve benefits of using the siwak according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal*, this hadith elevates the Sunnah of siwak from mere hygiene to a spiritual act that invites angelic presence and multiplies rewards, linking physical purity with divine pleasure. The comparison of two rak'ahs with siwak to seventy without it underscores the Shia emphasis on minor acts of worship as means of spiritual elevation, reflecting the holistic view of the body as a vessel for worship.
